rows.reason: Supply-chain insertion adds code before flight; ENISA's third party reads what retired media still hold.
Poisoned dependencies are inserted into live builds, not read from discarded media.
Software supply-chain compromise implants code; ENISA describes information obtained from disposed media.
Hardware tampering before delivery is the opposite end of the lifecycle from disposal.
Compromising a running SDR needs an operating radio, which a disposed medium is not.
Crosslink compromise needs a live neighbouring satellite.
A backup command channel exists only on an operating mission.
A standby ground station is a live system, not retired media.
The backup receiver is a live on-board path.
Rendezvous operations approach an active asset; nothing in ENISA's sentence describes approaching decommissioned infrastructure.
Emanation analysis needs an emitting system, which disposed media are not.
Docked-vehicle access targets an operating host.
Proximity grappling is physical contact with a flying vehicle; ENISA's third party holds discarded equipment.
The hosted-payload door is an operating-mission boundary.
Compromising a live ground system is not recovery of data from discarded media.
The on-orbit update pipeline is an operational path.
Commanding through a valid ground station needs an operating spacecraft.
A rogue external entity talks to an operating spacecraft.
A rogue ground station transmits to a commandable satellite.
A rogue spacecraft interacts with an active satellite.
An ASAT weapon destroys; ENISA describes data being read.
Trusted-relationship access rides a live partner connection.
Mission-collaborator access is to live systems.
Vendor remote access is to live systems.
The user segment is a live path into the mission.
Safe-mode access presumes a commandable spacecraft.
Auxiliary-device compromise targets a system in use.
ATLO compromise is a pre-launch path; disposal comes after operations.
Host-spacecraft compromise pivots from a hosted function on an active satellite.
Abusing native spacecraft functionality is an operating-spacecraft impact.
Forcing a state or mode change acts on a live spacecraft.
Altering configuration settings acts on a live system.
Falsifying or deleting data is modification; ENISA describes third parties obtaining data.
Altering command and data flows acts on an operating system.
Replacing software or firmware on a live spacecraft is not recovery of data from disposed media.
Resource exhaustion is denial of an operating service.
Timing manipulation acts on a running system.
Pivoting through a hosted payload needs an active host.
Hopping across crosslinks needs live vehicles.
